claim: The 237 s per-round floor is process + resident LOAD, so a persistent resident removes it.
pre_committed_kill: marginal cost of a second cycle in an already-warm process > 150 s would mean the floor is per-cycle and persistence does not help. Stated before measuring.
result: CONFIRMED at 60.7 s marginal. Three cycles cost 1.68x one cycle, not 3x.
PROJECTED_WIN: A 23-round ladder goes from ~68 min to ~25 min, 2.7x, on the campaign's dominant cost. For comparison, the MoE fusion fix shipped earlier this session is worth 2.0% of an 8.816 ms decode step.
VARIANCE_CAVEAT: The same one-cycle command measured 237.3 s earlier and 177.6 s here, a 34% spread. The absolute figures inherit that. What does NOT depend on it is the SHAPE: three cycles cost 1.68x one cycle within a single measurement pair, so most of a round is one-time setup no matter which absolute baseline is used. The 60.7 s marginal is far below the 150 s kill threshold with room to spare.
WHAT_IT_DOES_NOT_FIX: 60.7 s per cycle is still 2.8x the 21.35 s cost of a COMPLETE evaluated arm. Even with persistence, the loop spends more wall deciding than measuring. Persistence takes the ratio from 12.8x to 2.8x; it does not invert it.
NEXT: Where does the remaining 60.7 s go? That is prompt compilation, generation, and structured output repair -- none of it measured yet.
